name: Live in Chicago
description: Released in 1990 to support the 1989 Neon Hearts tour.
subtitle: The 1990 Tour EP (Recorded Before "The Crash")
linerNotes: Recorded at the Rosemont Horizon just weeks before the bus accident that changed everything. For years, this tape sat in the vault, too painful for the band to listen to.

Released in 1997 as a fan-club exclusive, it captures the band at the absolute peak of their "First Era" physical powers. They are playing the "plastic" pop hits of 1987–1989, but they are playing them with the ferocity of a garage band trying to break out of a cage.

studioArchives.title: Historical Context
studioArchives.content: This is the last official recording of Ryan O'Connell performing standing up. Later that year, on the night of December 10, 1990 on Interstate 81 Northbound at Mile Marker 98 (Exit 98, Newbern, Virginia), the band's 1988 Holt Freighter touring van was clipped on black ice.

studioArchives.title: The "Engine" Awakens
studioArchives.content: Listen closely to Evan and Tyler's rhythm section on this record. Stripped of the studio click-track, they play the songs 15 BPM faster and infinitely heavier than the album versions, foreshadowing the hard rock sound of their 1995 independent rebirth.

liveTranscript.title: The "Scream": Live Transcript
paragraphs: As the final, synth-heavy chord of "Light Up the Night" fades, the arena is deafening. 18,000 teenagers are screaming for the pop idols they see on MTV.

At center stage, Ryan O'Connell stands gripping the mic stand, chest heaving, drenched in sweat under the blinding pink and teal stage lights. He looks over at Cassidy behind her towering rack of keyboards, then back at Tyler and Evan. A rebellious, exhausted grin breaks across his face. He leans into the microphone—ignoring the teleprompter—and shouts over the roar:
liveTranscript.quote: CHICAGO! ARE YOU STILL WITH US?! ... We've got one more for you tonight! The suits in L.A. told us to keep it quiet, they told us to play it safe... SO TYLER, COUNT US IN AND LET'S BLOW THE ROOF OFF THIS PLACE!
liveTranscript.attribution: Cue the blistering, overdriven opening riff of "My Anchor Holds"
